                    ### Question
                    A 22-year-old woman comes to the physician for gradual worsening of her vision. Her father died at 40 years of age. She is 181 cm (5 ft 11 in) tall and weighs 69 kg (152 lb); BMI is 21 kg/m2. A standard vision test shows severe myopia. Genetic analysis shows an FBN1 gene mutation on chromosome 15. This patient is at greatest risk of mortality due to which of the following causes?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Obstruction of the superior vena cava lumen
opb. Increased pressure in the pulmonary arteries
opc. Eccentric ventricular hypertrophy
opd. Supraventricular tachyarrhythmia
ope. Intimal tear of the aortic root

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient has a mutation in the FBN1 gene, which is associated with Marfan syndrome, a connective tissue disorder. This condition is known to cause aortic root dilation, which significantly increases the risk of an intimal tear of the aortic root, leading to acute aortic dissection. This is the most common and life-threatening cardiovascular complication in Marfan syndrome, aligning with the consensus that patients with this condition are at greatest risk of mortality from aortic dissection. The retrieved evidence paths support this by linking aortic root dilation to acute aortic dissection, which can lead to shock and other severe outcomes. Other options, such as obstruction of the superior vena cava, increased pulmonary artery pressure, eccentric ventricular hypertrophy, and supraventricular tachyarrhythmia, are less commonly associated with mortality in Marfan syndrome compared to aortic dissection.
